top_story: Across the region, formal postwar and post-ceasefire frameworks are proving unable to protect civilians or stabilize governance. In Yemen, renewed fighting and rapid Houthi advances had displaced about 125,000 people by 17 September, pushing families into camps and signaling that front-line shifts are again reshaping daily survival. In Gaza, reconstruction is being absorbed into a system of war governance as continued bombardment empties ceasefire language of any restorative meaning, leaving civilian recovery structurally blocked. The 18 September US sentencing of former Syrian prison official Samir Ousman al-Sheikh to 60 years underscores a parallel reality: accountability is advancing abroad even as much of the region remains defined by enduring coercive rule and mass civilian vulnerability.
